Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 18*, artifact PDF p. 896 (text layer read column-aware from the PDF), body agreement 0.991; 1604 Vatican typical edition OCR at line 55380, agreement 0.594 (degraded-latin: corroboration only); 1570 Venice OCR at line 74227, agreement 0.745 (degraded-latin: corroboration only). Recorded limitation: Body agreement on normalised characters: 1862 0.895, 1922 Mame 0.991, Benziger 1962 0.987. The prayer stands in the 1922 Mame word for word apart from pointing, orthography and the length of the conclusion; that witness agrees with the 1962 body at 0.991 of its normalised characters, and no difference is shared by both public-domain witnesses, which is the test this lane used for a genuine textual variant. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on the whole-book text layer alone: the eight per-leaf page images this repository holds for the 1862 are Commons leaves n700-n725, which are printed pp. [31]-[56] of its Commune - the Virgins, the Dedication and the Saturday Masses of the Blessed Virgin - and this lane's formularies stand at printed pp. [1]-[25]. No 1862 word here was read from a page image. Where the 1862 text layer damages a word the difference is recorded above with the witness that supplies the same word at the same place; the letterforms were inferred, not read. the marginal number 4261 was recovered from the text layer where it had been split into two tokens inside the body the CMAA text layer drops the ornamental initial of the first word; the opening word is taken from this repository's own recorded incipit for this oration Not checked: the 1862 and Mame punctuation was compared only as printed by their recognisers, so comma-level pointing in those two witnesses is not evidence.
